subject: Opsify burst-sample sizing & KPI alignment
messages:
From: Rajesh Kumar <rk@opsify.ai>
To: karthik_iyer@redwood.ai, marissa_cole@redwood.ai
Cc: laura_bennett@redwood.ai
Date: Tue, 10 Nov 2027 16:12:00 -0800
Subject: Follow-up: burst sampling + SLO targets (post discovery)

Thanks again for the call earlier — good to meet the team. To make progress on sizing and a short pilot, here are the key performance constraints from Opsify: 

- Latency SLO: p95 end-to-end (user-perceived token arrival) <= 300 ms for streaming responses.
- Streaming behavior: server-sent events (token-by-token flush) with a 50ms max flush interval; clients are sensitive to jitter.
- Concurrency: up to 120 simultaneous streaming sessions at peak.
- Typical request shape: average tokens per request = 80, median QPS = 7 (steady).
- Peak pattern: bursts up to ~220 QPS lasting ~30-60 seconds for campaign-driven surges.
  - That corresponds to peak tokens/sec ~= 220 * 80 = 17,600 tokens/sec (approx).

As next steps we can:
1) share a 30-minute telemetry sample (edge timestamps, per-request token counts, client-id hash) so you can infer realistic batching and cache hit characteristics.
2) get a conservative sizing recommendation (hosted vs dedicated ballpark) and an estimated monthly delta for their expected traffic.
3) schedule a 30-min follow-up to review the sizing and check any config tradeoffs (quantization, prefix caching, model variant).

I'm attaching a short sample export from our logs and a small doc with the event name mappings. If you need a different sample format, happy to re-export.

Thanks,
Rajesh
Head of Platform
Opsify

Attachments: opsify_peak_sample.jsonl (sample), opsify_event_map.csv (referenced)
From: karthik_iyer@redwood.ai
To: Rajesh Kumar <rk@opsify.ai>
Cc: marissa_cole@redwood.ai, laura_bennett@redwood.ai
Date: Tue, 10 Nov 2027 18:03:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Follow-up: burst sampling + SLO targets (post discovery)

Rajesh — great summary, thanks. We can definitely work from the 30-minute sample you mentioned. Quick clarifications before we run a sizing pass:

- Can the sample include per-request: request_id, client_hash, tokens_in, tokens_out, timestamp_edge_received, response_finish_timestamp? The client_hash helps us simulate realistic prefix-cache locality without seeing PII.
- Confirm that the 220 QPS peak is simultaneous requests that are all streaming; or is that the sum of streaming + short sync calls?

Planned internal workflow on our side:
- Marissa will run an initial throughput simulation using your telemetry (we use a sampler that reconstructs streaming flows and computes continuous batching efficiency).
- I'll produce a conservative sizing note (expected GPU-equivalents, warm pool vs burst pool, and a hosted vs dedicated cost delta).
- We'll flag any immediate SLO risks (e.g., p95 >300ms for long-form requests) and propose mitigations (prefix caching, token chunking, model micro-batches).

Deliverables & timeline:
- Telemetry template attached -> please drop the sample into the template and upload the result. (See: opsify_telemetry_template.jsonl)
- Initial sizing + risk note: 3 business days after we receive the sample.
- Call to review: suggest Nov 18 or Nov 19, 30 min.

Looping Marissa and Laura to start the sizing exercise once we have the sample.

--
Karthik Iyer
Senior Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
From: marissa_cole@redwood.ai
To: karthik_iyer@redwood.ai
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>, Rajesh Kumar <rk@opsify.ai>
Date: Wed, 11 Nov 2027 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Follow-up: burst sampling + SLO targets (post discovery)

Rajesh / team — quick readout from a first-pass simulation assumptions (internal). I'll publish the CSV estimate (attached) with line-item math, but highlights here: 

Assumptions used for sizing:
- Model behavior: production open LLM (approx token-gen latency 0.8 - 1.5 ms/token on optimized kernels for non-streaming); streaming overhead and flush windows add ~30-70ms headroom.
- Client pattern: avg tokens/request = 80, median QPS steady = 7, peak bursts = 220 QPS x 60s.
- Streaming concurrency mapping: 120 concurrent streams during peak window => sustained concurrency affects KV cache memory more than pure GPU throughput.

Sizing back-of-envelope (conservative):
- Steady-state: ~0.6k tokens/sec -> fits comfortably in a single inference node with continuous batching and prefix cache.
- Burst headroom: 17.6k tokens/sec peak -> to hit p95 <= 300ms with streaming flushes we recommend an initial config of:
  - 3 inference GPUs in the warm pool (handle steady + batching) + 2 burst GPUs (autoscale to absorb the 30-60s surges).
  - Use model quantization profile Q8-fast for burst nodes to increase throughput with modest p95 impact.

Risk notes & optimization levers: 
- If peak bursts are dominated by long-form requests (tokens/request > 300) per-request latency can push p95 above 300ms; in that case we recommend:
  1) enable client-side token chunking (stream smaller pieces) and server-side streaming micro-batches,
  2) aggressive prefix caching for repeated system prompts,
  3) fall back to a slightly lower-capacity but lower-latency model for short prompts to reduce pressure.

Next steps for us and for you:
- Rajesh: please upload the 30-minute telemetry JSONL into the template and flag any redactions.
- Once we have the sample we will: (a) run the simulator, (b) produce a sizing spreadsheet with estimated monthly cost comparison (hosted vs dedicated), and (c) prepare a short slide for the review call.

Attaching: initial-sizing-estimate.csv (contains the spreadsheet math and recommended warm/burst counts).

Thanks — Marissa
Principal Performance Solutions, Redwood Inference
From: Rajesh Kumar <rk@opsify.ai>
To: marissa_cole@redwood.ai, karthik_iyer@redwood.ai
Cc: laura_bennett@redwood.ai
Date: Tue, 16 Nov 2027 09:22:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Follow-up: burst sampling + SLO targets (post discovery)

Thanks Karthik & Marissa — appreciate the quick read. I've uploaded the actual 30-minute sample as requested (opsify_peak_sample.jsonl) to the Drive folder you shared, and attached a trimmed copy here.

A few clarifications after a quick look at your note:
- The 220 QPS peak is indeed primarily streaming sessions. We do see a small fraction (~15%) of synchronous calls during bursts.
- Token distribution is skewed: ~70% of requests are short (< 60 tokens), ~25% mid (60-250), ~5% long (>250).

Would you be able to: 
1) confirm if the proposed "3 warm + 2 burst" sizing meets p95 <= 300ms for the heavy-tail token mix; and
2) give us a rough hosted vs dedicated monthly delta (order of magnitude) so our procurement team can triage budget.

We can do the review call on Nov 18 at 10am PT if that works — please confirm and I will send a calendar invite.

Appreciate the help,
Rajesh
Head of Platform, Opsify

Attachments: opsify_peak_sample.jsonl
